newsitem.title: CANADA: Rogers shares gain as asset sale welcomed.
newsitem.headline: Rogers shares gain as asset sale welcomed.

text.p: Shares in Rogers Communications Inc rose in New York and Toronto on Thursday as investors gave the company's sale of some Ontario cable systems a warm reception.
On Wednesday, Rogers agreed to sell some Ontario cable systems for C$350 million to Quebec-based Cogeco Cable Inc .
The systems serve 300,000 subscribers in Hamilton, Niagara Falls, St. Catharines, Sarnia, Wallaceburg, Peterborough, the Ottawa Valley, Cornwall and North Bay.
Rogers shares were up 0.65 at 10.25 in Toronto, off the high of 10.45, and rose 1/4 to 7-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange after hitting a session peak of 7-3/4.
"It looks like a good (deal), a good price," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
He said that Rogers must take more action to shovel its way from under its heavy debt load, which totaled C$4.7 billion at June 30 this year.
"But this is definitely a step in the right direction," the analyst added.
The sale involves systems in Hamilton, Niagara Falls, St. Catharines, Sarnia, Wallaceburg, Peterborough, the Ottawa Valley, Cornwall and North Bay.
Most of these systems were acquired in the 1994 takeover of Maclean Hunter Ltd.
Analysts were upbeat about the deal, which will raise the amount of money realized by Rogers from asset sales in recent months to roughly C$760 million.
According to one analyst, Cogeco Cable is paying about nine to 10 times earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the cable systems.

"We are calculating that Rogers would be worth C$13 to C$15 a share at the valuations just paid by Cogeco and that Rogers doesn't require further asset sales until into 1998," said Jim Doak, director and senior vice-president of invesment research at ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
He said the upper-level valuation assumes that Rogers remaining subscribers are valued on the basis of 10 times EBITDA and that the traditional holding company discount is removed from the equation.
Holding companies are often traded at a significant discount to the value of their operating units.

"There's going to be more good news coming. The November conference on (Rogers') third quarter, will show improved margins for their cable business," said Jim Doak, director and senior vice-president of investment research at ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
